comparison.objective: Hold an oyster level, insert and twist a knife at its hinge, sever the muscle, remove the top shell, and discard it; candidate adjusts, locks, and dynamically validates an industrial-axis damper.
comparison.physical_skill: Bimanual restraint with blade insertion into a 4 mm gap, twisting, cutting, and safety clearance versus hex-key engagement, counterholding, controlled collar rotation, bounded tightening, guarded control actuation, and iterative force-response adjustment.
comparison.success_condition: Oyster task requires hinge release before lifting, muscle separation, level cup, holding hand at least 3 cm from the knife tip, knife laid down, and shell placed in a bowl; candidate requires two compliant stop cycles with specified travel, energy, velocity, rebound, overload, hard-stop, and setting-retention constraints. The record lacks numeric level tolerance, exact muscle-release measurement, final hold duration, and broader damage/spill thresholds.
comparison.reason: Although both use bimanual tool manipulation and twisting, oyster shucking tests constrained cutting and food handling, while the candidate tests mechanical adjustment, torque retention, and closed-loop commissioning from repeated impacts.
